title: Microsoft Purview Insider Risk Management: alerts in Microsoft Defender XDR
summary: The roadmap facts, sharing control, role-group command and documented investigation behaviour are supported. Remove the unsupported claim that alerts were previously visible only to IRM role groups, and reconcile the governance checklist with the controls table.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Microsoft plans to surface IRM alerts in Defender XDR unified alert and incident queues.
claims.quote: IRM alerts will be surfaced in unified alert and Incident queue in Microsoft Defender XDR.

claims.where: summary; What's changing
claims.claim: The planned advanced hunting experience exposes alerts, indicators and enriched events for KQL queries.
claims.quote: IRM alerts, Indicators and enriched events will be available in Microsoft Defender XDR advanced hunting. Analysts can leverage KQL queries to identify potentially hidden risky patterns in data security related user activity.

claims.where: summary; What's changing
claims.claim: The roadmap plans Graph API exposure of IRM alerts, indicators and enriched events.
claims.quote: IRM alert, Indicators and enriched events will be exposed through Graph API.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; controls[0].note; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The roadmap names Share data with Microsoft Defender XDR in IRM settings as the enabling setting.
claims.quote: This feature can be enabled through “Share data with Microsoft Defender XDR” within Microsoft Insider Risk Management settings

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: IRM data in Defender XDR does not honour anonymisation, exposing user identities.
claims.quote: IRM data in Microsoft Defender XDR does not honor anonymization.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Removing anonymisation enables correlation with alerts from solutions such as Defender for Endpoint and Defender for Cloud Apps.
claims.quote: This is to enable effective correlation of IRM alerts with alerts from other solutions in Microsoft Defender XDR platform (such as Defender for Endpoint, Defender for Cloud apps, etc.).

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; Governance controls
claims.claim: The feature requires administrator-enabled data sharing, supporting admin-opt-in.
claims.quote: Data sharing with other security solutions must be turned on in the Data sharing settings in Microsoft Purview Insider Risk Management.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The sharing control is in Microsoft Purview portal > Settings > Insider Risk Management > Data sharing > Sharing data with other Microsoft security solutions.
claims.quote: Select Settings ... Select Insider Risk Management ... In Insider Risk Management settings, select the Data sharing setting. Under the Sharing data with other Microsoft security solutions section, turn on the setting.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: No API or PowerShell operation for changing the Data sharing setting is documented at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: IRM Data sharing Defender XDR PowerShell Set-InsiderRiskManagementConfig Graph API; site:learn.microsoft.com/powershell insider sharing Set; Graph Purview insiderRiskManagement settings update. Read share-data and Graph search results; no operation sets this toggle.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: IRM group membership is edited in Microsoft Purview portal > Settings > Roles and groups > Roles groups > Insider Risk Management > Edit > Choose users.
claims.quote: Select Settings in the upper-right corner of the page, select Roles and groups, then select Roles groups in the left navigation pane. Select the Insider Risk Management role group, then select Edit. Select Choose users

claims.where: controls[1].api; controls[1].note; Governance controls table
claims.claim: Add-RoleGroupMember -Identity "<role-group>" -Member "<user-UPN>" adds a member to a management role group.
claims.quote: Use the Add-RoleGroupMember cmdlet to add members to a management role group. The Identity parameter specifies the role group to add a member to. User ID or user principal name (UPN)

claims.where: controls[1].governs; Governance controls
claims.claim: IRM role-group membership governs access to alerts and configuration of settings.
claims.quote: Access & investigate alerts | Yes | No | Yes | Yes | No | No; Configure policies and settings | Yes | Yes | No | No | No | No

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope; Governance controls
claims.claim: Access to IRM alerts in Defender requires Security Operator or Security Reader permissions.
claims.quote: The following permissions are essential to access insider risk management alerts in the Microsoft Defender portal: Security Operator; Security Reader

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope; Governance controls
claims.claim: Viewing and managing IRM alerts in Defender additionally requires membership in Insider Risk Management, Insider Risk Management Analysts or Insider Risk Management Investigators.
claims.quote: You must also be a member of one of the following insider risk management role groups to view and manage insider risk management alerts in the Microsoft Defender portal: Insider Risk Management; Insider Risk Management Analysts; Insider Risk Management Investigators

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Advanced hunting access to insider-risk data requires Insider Risk Management Analyst or Insider Risk Management Investigator.
claims.quote: To access insider risk data in advanced hunting, users must have the following Microsoft Purview Insider Risk Management roles: Insider Risk Management Analyst; Insider Risk Management Investigator

claims.where: Scope; Risk assessment: Data exposure

claims.quote: Customers integrating insider risk management alerts with other security information and events management (SIEM) tools using the Microsoft Graph security API must have the following permissions to successfully access the relevant Microsoft Defender data through APIs:

claims.where: What's changing
claims.claim: Learn describes IRM alerts related to a user correlated into a single incident.
claims.quote: Insider risk management alerts related to a user are correlated to a single incident to ensure a holistic approach to incident response.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The incident and alert queues can be filtered by Microsoft Purview Insider Risk Management under Service source.
claims.quote: You can filter incidents by choosing Microsoft Purview Insider Risk Management under Service source. All insider risk management alerts are also visible in the Microsoft Defender portal's alert queue. Filter these alerts by choosing Microsoft Purview Insider Risk Management under Service source.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Graph security API exposes IRM incidents, alerts and hunting data for integration with Microsoft Sentinel, ServiceNow and Splunk.
claims.quote: Use the Microsoft Graph security API to integrate insider risk management alerts, insights, and indicators with other SIEM tools like Microsoft Sentinel, ServiceNow, or Splunk.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Alert status updates sync between portals, so resolving an alert in Defender can change its IRM status.
claims.quote: Resolved | Classification dependent. If classification is not available, the alert status is set to Dismissed by default. Any updates made to an insider risk management alert in the Microsoft Purview or the Microsoft Defender portals are automatically reflected in both portals.

claims.claim: Severity updates are reflected in both portals.
claims.quote: Any updates made to an insider risk management alert in the Microsoft Purview or the Microsoft Defender portals are automatically reflected in both portals. These updates might include: Alert status; Severity; Activity that generated the alert; Trigger information; Classification

claims.where: What's changing
claims.claim: Alert generation or updates are reflected in both portals within 30 minutes.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions
claims.claim: A separate licence specific to the sharing setting is not published, and the Defender page names none.

claims.where: What's changing; Scope; controls[0].note; Open questions
claims.claim: The cited Learn pages do not specify the integration's government-cloud availability or start date.
claims.quote: Searched: IRM share data Defender XDR GCC GCC High DoD availability licensing charge meter. Read irm-investigate-alerts-defender, settings-share-data and defender-xdr/usgov; none states an IRM integration cloud-specific rollout date or availability.

claims.where: Why it matters
claims.claim: Before this change, the alerts were seen only by IRM role groups.
claims.quote: Searched: Insider Risk Management alerts access role groups export previously Defender XDR. Read permissions, integration, share-data and scc-permissions excerpts. They describe present roles and existing export routes, not historical visibility limited to IRM role groups.
claims.fix: Replace 'Alerts that were seen only by IRM role groups can be correlated with other detections and queried in bulk' with 'IRM alerts can be correlated with other detections and queried in bulk'.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft warns Sentinel automation can fail because IRM incidents have no alert content.
claims.quote: If you are using automation on Microsoft Sentinel incidents, note that automation risks failure due to insider risk management incidents having no alert content.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: Microsoft recommends the IRM Microsoft Sentinel data connector to obtain IRM alerts in Sentinel.
claims.quote: We recommend Microsoft Sentinel customers to use the Microsoft Purview Insider Risk Management – Microsoft Sentinel data connector to get insider risk management alerts in Microsoft Sentinel.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Every control the governance checklist asks readers to review or take stock of has a controls-table row.
claims.quote: Identify Microsoft Sentinel automation rules that act on incidents ... Check which Defender and Graph integrations ... would receive IRM alerts. The table contains only Data sharing and IRM role-group membership.
claims.fix: The Before rollout steps about Sentinel automation rules and Defender/Graph integrations have no matching controls-table rows. Remove those two checklist bullets; retain the existing Sentinel warning and Graph integration explanation in Risk assessment.
